newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama president says nation ready to run canal.
newsitem.headline: Panama president says nation ready to run canal.

text.p: Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares said on Saturday his nation is ready to take over operations of the Panama Canal as the final countdown to the turnover nears.

"In 1,000 days, one era ends and another begins. Today 92 percent of the personnel is Panamanian and the administration is Panamanian. Better said, we are more than prepared," said Perez Balladares at an official ceremony broadcast live to the nation from the presidential Palace of the Herons.
Under treaties signed in 1977, the United States will hand over control of the 52-mile (84 km) transoceanic waterway to Panama at noon on Dec. 31, 1999.
Perez Balladares said the first draft of the Canal Authority law has passed Congress and final passage is expected this year, "30 months before the canal is transferred over."

In his speech, Perez Balladares also sought to boost national moral, saying the Panamanian canal transition team working on the Canal Authority law is competent and will ensure the nation is ready to run the canal.

"There is such a terrible fear of failure that exists in the bosom of the Panamanian society that we don't believe we're capable or confident of handling the responsabilities that lay ahead," he said.

"These are the same pessimistic voices who doubted that the United States would go ahead with the (canal) treaties. You (the transition team) offer a huge security to the country that the canal in Panamanian hands will be administered with even better efficiency," he said.
